text:
lena: Short thought: we need a formal error-contract versioning signal so SDKs and the console can behave differently during rollouts. today clients just see 429/500 and react inconsistently.

chris: Agreed. Minimal, non-breaking approach = headers + telemetry. header sketch: `X-RW-Err-Ver: v1` and `X-RW-Err-Cat: quota|throttle|billing|degraded` and `X-RW-Err-Act: retry|backoff|contact`

arjun: Console should render a per-route "error contract" badge showing current observed versions and a small graph for pct traffic per version. clickable link opens the mapping rules and migration notes.

lena: Also emit `error_contract.observed` telemetry events with labels: route, observed_ver, client_version (when known), count. That will help detect old clients.

chris: SDK change: expose `onErrorContract(version, meta)` and a helper `recommendedAction(err)` that maps the header to an enum for apps. mobile apps can show an upgrade prompt when we detect older client versions failing.

arjun: For proxies that strip headers, fall back to a compact `error_meta` field in the response body for non-200s. keep it tiny (<256B).

lena: Rollout plan proposal: 1) telemetry-only for two weeks, 2) canary header emission (5%), 3) console badge + deprecation banner when >5% new ver, 4) optional compatibility mapping toggle per-route for 30d grace.

ops-bot: deploy: feature/error-contract rolled to canary=5% in us-west.

chris: Action items: lena write short RFC (mapping table + examples), arjun mock console badge and graph, devex to add SDK hooks. Reconvene next Tue to review canary metrics. :thumbsup:
